newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds close little changed.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds close little changed.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed nearly unchanged in balanced trading on Thursday and traders said the market had reached an equilibrium.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.04 pct to 105.09
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.04 to 103.99
Volume was a moderate 163 million shekels.

"The market reached an equilibrium and it is expected to remain at the current level. Yields on long CPI-linked bonds will remain in the near term at 4 to 4.1 percent," said Ilan Doron, head of trading at Solid Financial Markets.
A trader at the First International Bank of Israel (FIBI) predicted that inflation-linked bonds would continue to rise with falling yields.

"These bonds made a big move and now they need to rest. It's only a question of time before yields will start falling again. I belive that yields will eventualy fall to only 3.5 percent," the FIBI trader said.

Israel Discount Bank said in a report released on Tuesday that interest rates would fall by 0.5 percentage point during the second quarter due to a slowing economy but would hold steady in the third quarter.
Unlinked bonds were also stable and traders said they are expected to remain at current levels in the short term.
Makams rose slightly but volume fell to only 33 million shekels. "The rise of the dollar has a negative impact on the Makam because it will eventually lead to rising inflation," the FIBI trader said.

Dollar-linked bonds continued their rally as the shekel weakened against the U.S. currency. In local trading the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3930 shekels against 3.3900 on Wednesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
